title: Take a 2x photo with an iPhone 16's Camera Control: light-press to open zoom, slide to 2x without clicking, then click
instruction: Use the phone's Camera Control to take a photo at 2x zoom.
context: Most adults take photos with their phone and zoom in to frame a subject. On iPhone 16 and later, zoom and shutter are one 17 mm button: Apple's guide says a light press shows the setting, sliding a finger along the control adjusts it, and a click takes the photo. The knack is force on one small button: press lightly (about 0.5 N), slide about 6 mm without reaching the click (2 N), then click. Pressing straight down, or sliding too hard, takes the photo at 1x.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights are above the table. Apple iPhone 16 (white): 14.76 x 7.16 x 0.78 cm, 170 g, aluminium frame and glass faces, Camera app open at 1x, Zoom the Camera Control's saved setting. It stands in landscape with the screen to the arms and its top end (cameras) to the left, leaning back 15 degrees; centre at (30.0, 0.0), 5.5 cm up; lower edge 2.0 cm up. The Camera Control (17.1 x 0.3 cm sapphire) is on the top edge, centred at (31.0, -2.2), 9.1 cm up. Stand: aluminium desk stand, base 8.5 x 11 x 1.8 cm from x 26.5 to 35.0, y -5.5 to 5.5; silicone ledge 11 cm wide with a 3 mm front lip; back rest 9 x 4.5 cm, reclined 15 degrees. Photo subject (not scored, loose): slice of chocolate cake, SimReady food_prepared_cake_a01, 8.6 x 10.4 x 7.0 cm, 100 g, at (56, 6), turned 23 degrees. Distractors (SimReady, loose, not scored): ceramic mug dishware_mug_a01, 11.4 x 9.0 x 8.0 cm, 300 g, at (24, 24), turned 126 degrees; eyeglasses accessory_eyeglasses_a01, 14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, 30 g, at (50, -24), turned 69 degrees. Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read from the phone's latest photo and the phone's pose (real trial: the photo's Info in Photos, and 60 fps video; README). A click takes a photo at the zoom the dial shows; the dial reads exactly 2x (52 mm) from 1.80x to 2.22x. A photo is spoiled if, at the click, the phone moved faster than 2 cm/s or turned faster than 10 degrees/s, or a fingertip point was within 1.5 cm of a rear lens's centre. 1.0: the latest photo is unspoiled and at 2x, the phone rests in its stand (within 5 mm and 3 degrees of its start, moving under 1 cm/s and 3 degrees/s) and every fingertip point of both grippers is at least 3 cm from the phone, all held 1 s; scored 1.0 from then on. 0.75: the latest photo is unspoiled and at 2x, but the full conditions are not met. 0.5: the latest photo is unspoiled at 1.5x to 3.0x, other than 2x. 0.25: the latest photo is unspoiled at any other zoom. 0: no photo, or the latest photo is spoiled, or the phone was ever moved more than 2 cm or turned more than 10 degrees from its start before full credit.
reset_notes: Note the time of the latest photo (or delete the trial's photos). Lightly press the Camera Control and slide back to 1x, so the Camera app is at 1x with Zoom still the saved setting. Set the phone back in the stand against its tape marks. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Phone: a rigid box at the iPhone 16's size and mass with a sprung cap for the Camera Control. Its force sensor is read from cap travel (2,500 N/m: light press 0.5 N, click 2 N, estimates); the cap stands 2 mm proud (real: flush) so a rigid pad can press it. Touch is cap contact plus finger position along it; zoom per mm of slide (6 mm per doubling) and the 2x detent are estimates. The screen is coloured patches. Stand: primitives. Cake, mug, glasses: SimReady. Uniform friction.
